definition: TabPFN (Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network) is a machine learning model for tabular datasets proposed in 2022.
details: It uses a transformer architecture. It is intended for supervised classification and regression analysis on tabular datasets, particularly focusing on small- to medium-sized datasets. The latest version, TabPFN-3, was released in May 2026 and supports datasets with up to one million rows and 200 features.

explainer.lead: TabPFN is a transformer-based machine learning model for tabular datasets, proposed in 2022, aimed at supervised classification and regression. It matters for small- to medium-sized tabular problems.

tiers.eli5: Like a prediction helper built specifically for spreadsheets, guessing outcomes from rows of data.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to tabular classification and regression, especially small- to medium-sized datasets; the pitfall is the dataset size ceiling.
tiers.paperLevel: A prior-data fitted network using a transformer architecture for supervised classification and regression on tabular data, focused on small- to medium-sized datasets; TabPFN-3 supports up to one million rows and 200 features.

explainer.example: A tabular dataset within the supported limits is passed to TabPFN-3, which returns classification predictions.
